change.title: 10 changes: Coinbase Pro API (api.pro.coinbase.com) deprecated; callers must move to the Exchange API (api.exchange.coinbase.com) and more

source.quote: The Pro API ([https://api.pro.coinbase.com](https://api.pro.coinbase.com)) has been deprecated. For REST API access, leverage the [Exchange API]

tasks.reasoning:
This one task covers all 10 coinbase-pro changes that affect this repo. Handle every one of them in this single change set, prove each with your test, and say in finish which you changed and which needed no change.

1. Coinbase Pro API (api.pro.coinbase.com) deprecated; callers must move to the Exchange API (api.exchange.coinbase.com) (product-shutdown, effective 2024-09-11)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md
   Quote: The Pro API ([https://api.pro.coinbase.com](https://api.pro.coinbase.com)) has been deprecated. For REST API access, leverage the [Exchange API]
   Affects: operations: api.pro.coinbase.com
   Call sites: coinbaseProLibrary.js:106 (GET /profiles is sent over HTTP to the apiURI base (api.pro.coinbase.com), which is deprecated; it must point at api.exchange.coinbase.com.); coinbaseProLibrary.js:152 (GET /fees uses the same deprecated Pro base URL.); coinbaseProLibrary.js:210 (POST /profiles/transfer uses the same deprecated Pro base URL.); strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js:46 (AuthenticatedClient is built with the Pro apiURI (api.pro.coinbase.com); all SDK REST calls (placeOrder, getOrder, cancelOrder, getAccounts, getProducts, getAccount) go to the deprecated host.); strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js:81 (WebsocketClient uses the Pro feed (ws-feed.pro.coinbase.com), which belongs to the deprecated Pro stack and needs the Exchange feed (ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com).); strategies/momentumTradingWithStopLoss/momentumTradingWithStopLoss.js:82 (Websocket ticker feed uses the Pro host.); strategies/reverseMomentumTrading/reverseMomentumTrading.js:81 (Websocket ticker feed uses the Pro host.); buyAndSell.js:57 (Order placement goes through the authedClient pointed at the deprecated Pro API.)
   Why it applies: The repo hard-codes api.pro.coinbase.com, the sandbox Pro host and the ws-feed.pro hosts in both the coinbase-pro SDK usage (0.9.0, an unmaintained package) and the hand-rolled axios client. The Pro API has been deprecated since 2024-09-11, so calls may already fail or stop working. The migration agent should change the REST base URLs (prod and sandbox) to api.exchange.coinbase.com / api-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com and the websocket URIs to ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com / ws-feed-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com. It should also check that the coinbase-pro SDK accepts the new URIs, or replace it, and that the CB-ACCESS auth still works with the existing keys. Keys created on Pro may need to be reissued on Exchange.

2. Travel rule fields being removed from POST /withdrawals/crypto; withdraw only to allowlisted addresses (date unclear) (field-removed)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/upcoming-changes.md
   Quote: We are removing travel rule fields from `POST /withdrawals/crypto` REST API.
   Affects: operations: POST /withdrawals/crypto
   Why it applies: Not applicable to any call site.

3. Coinbase Exchange domain only accepts TLS 1.2 or higher (other, effective 2025-10-20)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md
   Quote: This means that any client applications, trading bots, or other automated systems that currently rely on older versions of TLS (such as TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1) will no longer be able to establish a secure connection with the Coinbase Exchange domain.
   Why it applies: The match agent returned no verdict for this change. Check the repo for any use of it, then migrate or conclude not affected.

4. MiCA-regulated Exchange customers must switch to MiCA-specific REST, FIX and WebSocket hosts (other, effective 2025-12-11)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md
   Quote: Coinbase Exchange customers subject to the EU Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation must transition to MiCA-specific Coinbase Exchange URLs.
   Affects: operations: https://api-us.dma.prime.coinbase.com, wss://ws-us.dma.prime.coinbase.com
   Why it applies: The match agent returned no verdict for this change. Check the repo for any use of it, then migrate or conclude not affected.

5. Address book network field accepts _ALL_EVM_NETWORKS_ (only with currency _ALL_ASSETS_); currencies adds is_evm_network (additive, verify) (other, effective 2026-02-02)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md
   Quote: A new value of `_ALL_EVM_NETWORKS_` has been added to the `network` field in the address book endpoints. This value is only valid when the currency is `_ALL_ASSETS_`.
   Affects: operations: POST /address-book; fields: network, is_evm_network
   Why it applies: The match agent returned no verdict for this change. Check the repo for any use of it, then migrate or conclude not affected.

6. FIX Drop Copy now delivers execution reports for new/changed/cancelled/stop-limit activation orders; FIX OE delivers prior-session ERs (behaviour change) (other, effective 2025-10-30)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md
   Quote: Execution Reports (ER) will be delivered for `cancelled` and `Stop-Limit activation` orders.
   Why it applies: The match agent returned no verdict for this change. Check the repo for any use of it, then migrate or conclude not affected.

7. FIX execution reports no longer include SenderSubID (50)=TEST (other, effective 2026-03-12)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/upcoming-changes.md
   Quote: we will be deploying a change to our FIX engines to remove the SenderSubID (50) = TEST that is returned on every execution report from the exchange.
   Affects: fields: SenderSubID (50)
   Why it applies: The match agent returned no verdict for this change. Check the repo for any use of it, then migrate or conclude not affected.

8. FIX OrderCancelBatch (U4) by ClOrdID for nonexistent order now returns OrderCancelBatchReject (U5) (other, effective 2026-09-25)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/upcoming-changes.md
   Quote: Going forward, such requests will receive an explicit OrderCancelBatchReject (U5).
   Affects: operations: OrderCancelBatch (U4), OrderCancelBatchReject (U5)
   Why it applies: The match agent returned no verdict for this change. Check the repo for any use of it, then migrate or conclude not affected.

9. Transfer funds between profiles now returns transfer_id instead of an empty 200 body (other, effective 2026-10-13)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/upcoming-changes.md
   Quote: The [Transfer funds between profiles)](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/exchange-api/rest-api/profiles/transfer-funds-profile.md) REST endpoint now returns the `transfer_id` in a 200 successful response. Previously, we returned an empty 200 response.
   Affects: fields: transfer_id
   Why it applies: The match agent returned no verdict for this change. Check the repo for any use of it, then migrate or conclude not affected.

10. Opt-in portfolio isolation for API keys: keys without cross portfolio access get limited results/403/404 (release TBD) (auth-change)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/upcoming-changes.md
   Quote: When on, keys without **cross portfolio access** are limited to their own portfolio.
   Affects: operations: GET /profiles, GET /accounts/all
   Why it applies: The match agent returned no verdict for this change. Check the repo for any use of it, then migrate or conclude not affected.

record.prBody:
## 10 changes: Coinbase Pro API (api.pro.coinbase.com) deprecated; callers must move to the Exchange API (api.exchange.coinbase.com) and more [Verified]

### Change

Swapped Pro hosts for Exchange hosts (REST and websocket, real and sandbox) in the 3 strategy files. These constants feed both the SDK clients and the axios helper. Updated the README docs links. buyAndSell.js now logs the profile transfer result as JSON plus transfer_id. Added test_hosts.js, a static check.

Files touched:
- `README.md`
- `buyAndSell.js`
- `strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js`
- `strategies/momentumTradingWithStopLoss/momentumTradingWithStopLoss.js`
- `strategies/reverseMomentumTrading/reverseMomentumTrading.js`
- `test_hosts.js`

### Why

api.pro.coinbase.com and ws-feed.pro are deprecated. The Exchange API is the successor, with the same paths and auth.

> The Pro API ([https://api.pro.coinbase.com](https://api.pro.coinbase.com)) has been deprecated. For REST API access, leverage the [Exchange API]

Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hosts | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- hosts, added by the agent: `node test_hosts.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `hosts`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Live connectivity, HMAC signing and the private endpoints on the Exchange hosts
- The sandbox host names were not confirmed in the docs
- The coinbase-pro SDK (0.9.0) is abandoned and was left in place
- Existing Pro keys may need to be reissued on Exchange
- The test is static and does not run the code
- Changes 2 and 4-8 (the withdrawal travel-rule fields, FIX changes, MiCA hosts, address book) need no change because the repo does not use those endpoints. MiCA hosts were not added; they are opt-in for MiCA customers. Change 3 (TLS 1.2 minimum) was not checked in code. Node's defaults already require TLS 1.2 or higher.
- Change 10 (portfolio isolation) could limit GET /profiles results for keys without cross-portfolio access. The code was not changed for it.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- All REST and websocket traffic now goes to Exchange hosts
- The transfer log line now prints JSON and transfer_id, because POST /profiles/transfer now returns {transfer_id}. The helper already returned result.data, so it is unchanged.

---

preparation.reasoning: Plain Node.js project with no codegen, build, or workspace packages. package.json has no postinstall/prepare/generate scripts, the test script is a placeholder, and no checks were detected. Dependencies are already installed, so nothing further is needed.

review.summary: The diff swaps the host constants in three strategy files from Pro to Exchange, which is the core of the API change, and the new test_hosts.js confirms those strings. The grade 'verified' rests only on a static grep/string test, not on any request to Exchange. Several named call sites are not visibly handled. coinbaseProLibrary.js (GET /profiles, GET /fees, POST /profiles/transfer) is not in the diff. It receives apiURI through its constructor, so it probably follows the new host. I could not confirm that from the quoted files, and I could not confirm that the Exchange API accepts the same paths and response shapes. The bot also still depends on the deprecated coinbase-pro npm package for WebsocketClient and AuthenticatedClient. The package's signing and auth against the Exchange host are untested here, and so is the websocket feed. buyAndSell.js has an unrelated logging change: a debug line that now prints JSON.stringify(transferResult) plus transfer_id. It has an indentation glitch (an extra leading space). Its justification is unclear, and test_hosts.js now asserts on it. If profileTransfer returns something different on Exchange, the log is the only place that would surface it. A stray test_hosts.js sits in the repo root and is not wired into package.json. It only greps source text. README link updates are fine. The sandbox hostnames (api-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com and the ws-feed-public.sandbox equivalent) are not something I can confirm from memory, so check them against the Exchange sandbox docs. The README's 'Running the program out of sandbox' text may also be stale, which is pre-existing.

concerns.issue: The only check is a static string test. No call (getAccounts, getProducts, placeOrder, websocket subscribe) was run against Exchange or its sandbox. The 'verified' grade overstates what the checks prove. The same applies to the other two strategy files.

This file is named as an affected call site (GET /profiles, /fees, POST /profiles/transfer) but is not changed. It likely inherits the host from the apiURI constructor argument. Confirm it does not hard-code the Pro host or Pro-specific paths and headers, and that the Exchange endpoints and response shapes match.

The deprecated coinbase-pro npm library still handles auth, the REST calls and the WebsocketClient. Pointing it at the Exchange host is not shown to work. Check the websocket auth and subscribe message against the Exchange feed docs.

This logging change goes beyond what the API change requires. It adds transfer_id and JSON.stringify, which assumes a response field not confirmed in the quoted source. The line also has an extra leading space of indentation.
A throwaway grep-style test is committed to the repo root and is not wired into npm scripts. It also asserts on the unrelated log line in buyAndSell.js.

checkFirst: Run the bot or a script against the Exchange sandbox and confirm getAccounts, getProducts, getProfiles and a websocket ticker subscription succeed with the existing API keys.
Open coinbaseProLibrary.js and confirm it builds URLs from the passed apiURI with no hard-coded pro.coinbase hosts; compare its three endpoints with the Exchange reference.
Check the sandbox hostnames and the websocket feed URLs in the Exchange sandbox docs.
Check that the coinbase-pro package's request signing works unchanged against the Exchange host.
Confirm why the buyAndSell.js log line was changed and whether profileTransfer actually returns transfer_id.
